App details

Electrical Toolkit

Work out common electrical and electronic values from the measurements you enter.

In the worksPlannedAndroid

What it’s for

An offline helper for electronics projects and practical calculations. Enter voltage, current, resistance and component values to work out power, choose LED resistors, combine components or estimate voltage drop in a wire. You can also read resistor colour bands and printed codes.

Main features

  • Ohm’s law, power and component calculations.
  • Read resistor colour bands and printed codes.
  • Calculate resistor networks and LED resistors.
  • Wire resistance and voltage drop from entered data.

This app is being planned and is not yet available to download. The description presents its intended functions.

Features in detail

Circuits, components and practical calculations

Ohm’s law and power

Enter two known values among voltage, current and resistance to find the third. Power can be found from voltage/current, current/resistance or voltage/resistance. Results describe the entered ideal circuit values; they do not certify an electrical installation as safe.

Charge and reciprocal electrical quantities

Find charge from current×time or capacitance×voltage. Convert positive resistance to conductance and back, or material resistivity to conductivity and back. You supply the material’s value; no material or operating condition is assumed, and zero denominators are rejected.

AWG, wire resistance and voltage drop

Select an AWG wire size to see diameter and cross-section, or use the stated rounding rules for a reverse size suggestion. Enter conductor length, material resistivity, cross-section and current for resistance and voltage drop; specify one-way or return length. It does not select a safe current rating or protective device.

Series and parallel components

Choose resistance, capacitance or inductance, enter a list of positive component values and select series or parallel. See the equivalent total; add or remove list entries to compare arrangements. Inductor calculations assume no magnetic coupling. The result alone gives no voltage rating or thermal design.

Voltage divider and LED resistor

For an unloaded divider, enter input voltage and its two resistances to get output voltage. For a LED, enter supply voltage, LED forward voltage and desired current to find resistance and resistor heat loss. Suggested standard value avoids increasing the target current; a power class is estimated with stated margin, while real part limits still matter.

Resistor colours, SMD codes and capacitor codes

Choose four or five resistor bands for value, multiplier and tolerance, or obtain supported colours from a value. Decode 3/4-digit resistor markings and EIA-96 codes, with reverse codes when representable. Decode common 3-digit capacitor markings: 104 gives 100 nF. Unknown or ambiguous manufacturer codes are identified, not guessed.

Preferred standard component values

Choose E12, E24, E48 or E96 and enter a value to see the nearest, next lower and next higher preferred values at the relevant scale. This helps find a purchasable resistor value; the LED recommendation uses its current-limit rule rather than always choosing the nearest value.

Reactance, resonance and stored energy

Frequency plus capacitance or inductance gives capacitive or inductive reactance, the opposition to alternating current. Capacitance plus inductance gives ideal LC resonance frequency. A capacitor’s capacitance/voltage or an inductor’s inductance/current gives its stored energy. Enter each required value explicitly; these are ideal models.

RC time constant, charging and discharging

Enter resistance and capacitance to find the RC time constant. For charging or discharging, also enter the supply/starting voltage and elapsed time to find capacitor voltage and progress percentage. A valid target level can give required time. The model assumes ideal components and stated starting conditions.

NE555 single pulses and oscillation

Choose monostable mode for a single pulse: resistance and capacitance estimate its duration. Astable mode uses the classic resistor/capacitor arrangement for frequency, period, high/low times and duty percentage. The displayed circuit model matters; other arrangements and real chip tolerances may produce different results.

LM317 voltage and heat-loss estimate

Enter R1/R2 for output voltage, or desired output and fixed R1 for required R2. Input voltage, output voltage and load current estimate regulator dissipation. The stated reference-voltage model is used; this calculation does not decide heatsink suitability or replace chip datasheet limits.

Simple filters and star–delta networks

For RC low/high-pass or RL filters, enter the relevant component values to get cutoff frequency for the shown connection; ideal RLC gives resonance. For star↔delta, choose direction and enter three positive resistances to see three labelled equivalents preserving the nodes. These are basic ideal models, not complete filter or installation design.

Magic smoke

Tap the About logo seven times: a drawn LED gets brighter, flashes, smokes and goes out, illustrating the magic-smoke joke. This offline scene is not a wiring or safety demonstration and changes no calculation.

Use, settings and availability

Offline use

The main functions are designed to work on your device without a JN86 account. Ads, purchases and external links may need internet.

Language, settings and help

Choose one of eight app languages and adjust the available settings. About provides privacy information and a link to voluntary JN86 support. Support does not unlock paid functions. Availability is shown below.

Ads and optional ad removal

All described functions are planned to be free, with banner ads and optional one-time Google Play ad removal. No subscription is planned. The purchase screen shows the actual local price; purchase restoration uses Google Play.

Availability

This app is being created. The features described here are planned; it is not yet available to download.
